doubling_stock.criterion: every finite incident Coxeter order is even; in this exact diagram this is equivalent to having no incident m=3 edge

lineage_and_scope.allcock_mechanism: classical: Theorems 4.1 and 4.3 of Allcock, Infinitely many hyperbolic Coxeter groups through dimension 19, Geom. Topol. 10 (2006), 737-758, DOI 10.2140/gt.2006.10.737
lineage_and_scope.historical_H12_boundary: Allcock already proved infinitely and exponentially many finite-covolume H12 Coxeter examples using a Conway-face seed
lineage_and_scope.maximum_scope: maximality and uniqueness are only inside the exact 124 doubling walls of JK-H12-172; descendant walls, other seeds, and arbitrary reflection hyperplanes are not classified
lineage_and_scope.project_gain: the exact unique 112-wall disjoint and 96-wall ultraparallel maxima inside this surface-derived 124-wall doubling stock, together with full-Picard inheritance for every finite subtree

allcock_4_1_applicability.conclusion: every subtree union is a Coxeter polyhedron
allcock_4_1_applicability.hypotheses: Q is a Coxeter polytope and the selected walls are pairwise disjoint doubling walls

allcock_4_3_applicability.conclusion: the number of index-I reflection subgroups up to conjugacy by hyperbolic isometries, and hence the associated nonisometric finite-subtree polytopes, has an exponential lower bound in I
allcock_4_3_applicability.hypotheses: Q has finite volume and at least three pairwise disjoint doubling walls; in fact 96 are already pairwise ultraparallel

carrier.inheritance_reason: after translating a finite subtree to contain the identity chamber, every seed wall outside the selected generator stock remains an exterior wall; these displayed cores span the Picard lattice with index one.  Every other boundary root is an image of a primitive seed root under integral Picard isometries
carrier.scope: weak full-Picard divisor-reflection carrier only; no boundary root is asserted effective, no descendant is asserted to be a nef cone, and no Picard reflection is asserted to be a surface automorphism

theorem.disjoint_definition: the wall hyperplanes do not meet in H12; both parallel and ultraparallel pairs count, exactly as in Allcock's hypothesis
theorem.finite_subtree_statement: for k=112 (or k=96), let Gamma be the k-regular Cayley tree of the free product of k copies of C2 generated by the selected wall reflections.  Every finite subtree T gives a finite-sided, finite-volume, noncompact H12 Coxeter polytope Q_T
